tldr: The thread opened in late October with DocSkill, an arXiv paper applying skill-integrated agents to multilingual multi-hop document QA. LibriSpeech-Real-QA followed on Nov 4 with a benchmark for streaming speech QA, where models must answer before the full audio arrives.
whats_new: SAGE-QA (Nov 12) proposes semantic-aware, grounded scoring for SQuAD 2.0 closed-context QA, replacing character-level Exact Match with checks on whether answers are supported by the passage or correctly abstain.
why_it_matters: The thread has shifted from new QA methods to how QA is measured: if Exact Match misjudges grounded answers and abstentions, RAG eval suites built on it misreport faithfulness.

beats.headline: DocSkill brings skill-integrated agents to multilingual multi-hop document QA
beats.summary: Evidence must be located across pages, layouts and languages, which single-pass approaches handle poorly.

beats.headline: LibriSpeech-Real-QA benchmarks streaming question answering for speech LLMs
beats.summary: Targets speech models that only respond after the complete audio segment arrives.

beats.headline: SAGE-QA challenges Exact Match scoring for grounded, abstention-aware QA
beats.summary: Moves the thread from methods to evaluation: scoring support from the passage and correct abstention on SQuAD 2.0.

open_questions: Do any of these methods report results that hold up outside their own benchmarks?
Will speech LLMs show measurable accuracy loss when answering before the full audio arrives?
How far do SQuAD 2.0 model rankings move when scored with SAGE-QA instead of Exact Match?
Is SAGE-QA's grounding check released as code that can be dropped into an existing RAG eval harness?
take_for_builders: If your QA or RAG evals score with Exact Match, spot-check a sample of grounded paraphrases and abstentions by hand before trusting the metric; treat all three papers as preprints until reproduced.
